pos.personaBrief: Grêmio held about 51-53% possession and worked the ball well (Trivela, Goal), yet was lethal on the counter with Fernandinho's pace (Goal, Trivela, FIFA); possession was a means, not an end.

pro.personaBrief: Arthur was key to the saída de bola and Luan led the midfield, so build-up was constructive, but the team was vertical and fast in attack (Trivela, Goal).

est.personaBrief: A 4-2-3-1 inherited from Roger Machado with tactical obedience, but Luan roaming between the lines and Fernandinho and Luan approaching Barrios suggest a fairly relational attack; Barrios stayed in the box.

lar.personaBrief: Fast wide men (Fernandinho and Everton down the left, FIFA and Bola na Rede) were central to the plan, with Luan as the inside creator, so the width is real but the best talent sat centrally.

blo.personaBrief: The team pressed aggressively in the final and used high lines in the first half, though it lowered its lines late in games; it was not a deep-block team.

mar.personaBrief: Marking is undocumented, so this is memory-based: Brazilian sides of the period mostly defended by zone, with no known dedicated man-marker for stars.

pla.personaBrief: Renato kept the base 4-2-3-1 but tailored plans to opponents (speed against Pachuca's tall, slow defenders) and kept a plan B, so he adapts without dropping his style.

res.personaBrief: Trivela praised the most attractive football in Brazil, but the team won through solidity and counter-attacks and lowered its lines to close out the final.

sis.personaBrief: Tactical obedience was credited, yet Luan was the free-roaming brain of the team; the system rested on recovered players doing their jobs.

jog.personaBrief: A technical team (Luan, Arthur, Ramiro) with pace on the wings; Luan as a classic creator fits, and it was not built around physical duels.

bas.personaBrief: The squad was built on experienced players that others had written off (Barrios, Jael, Cícero, Léo Moura, Cortez), mixed with a few youngsters; titles came from veterans.

lid.personaBrief: Renato's strongest asset was his relationship with the squad: dialogue, no vanity crises despite constant rotation, and players recovered through trust, while still deciding himself.
